subject: Time to event analysis in DO mice

messages.author: 84f3288c7251590c
messages.subject: Time to event analysis in DO mice
parts: We would really like to use a time to event as our phenotype for GWAS of DO mice, but would have some mice that will not have the event. I can enter last day of the experiment for my phenotype, but was wondering if there was a different way to do this that incorporates the lack of event occurring in some mice. I don't think the binary approach would be as useful since only 10% of our mice never reach the event and there are several that have a long delay before the event. Does anyone have any advice? Thank you guys for your help.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Time to event analysis in DO mice
parts:
It maybe depends on whether the 10% that didn't reach the event are just censored or whether they were basically cured and would never have shown the event.

I guess I would start by just plugging in the maximum observed time. But you could also explore treating them as properly censored values, say in a Cox proportional hazards model. Or do the analysis of the quantitative trait among the mice with observed event values, and then the binary trait (event observed or not), along the lines of Broman 2003 https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/12663553 The overall sample size will have a big effect on things. Are we talking about 10% of 300 or of 600?

karl
